topic: Nitrogen vs. regular air for tire fill — is it worth it for a daily driver?

beats.vo: Paid extra for nitrogen in your tires? Here's what it actually does.
beats.visual: Macro shot of a green tire valve cap (the common nitrogen-fill marker) against a dark tire sidewall, static camera

beats.vo: Regular air is already about 78 percent nitrogen. The fill just pushes that closer to 95 percent or more.
beats.visual: Split-frame style comparison: two identical tire cutaway/valve close-ups side by side, subtle color-graded difference only, no on-screen text

beats.vo: The real benefit: nitrogen molecules are bigger, so they leak through the rubber a little slower, meaning slightly steadier pressure over time.
beats.visual: Extreme macro of tire sidewall rubber texture, slow push-in, ambient shop lighting

beats.vo: But it's not a substitute for checking your pressure. Even nitrogen-filled tires still lose pressure with cold weather.
beats.visual: Close-up of a tire pressure gauge being read at a valve stem, static mounted camera, no hands in frame, gauge needle/digits visible

beats.vo: Worth checking your pressure monthly either way. Stop by and we'll take a look.
